title: Turbulent averaging and open closure questions

items.title: Turbulent averaging and open closure questions
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring in progress; current item checkpoint recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $N\ge1$. For $j=1,\ldots,N$, let $u_j:I	imes\Omega	o\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ in $(t,x)$ with continuous second spatial derivatives, let $p_j:I	imes\Omega	o\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $f_j:I	imes\Omega	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous. Suppose $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$ and $$\partial_tu_j+\operatorname{div}(u_j\otimes u_j)+
abla p_j=
u\Delta u_j+f_j$$ for one common constant $
u\ge0$. Fix weights $a_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^N a_j=1$, define $ ar u=\sum_j a_ju_j$, $ ar p=\sum_j a_jp_j$, $ ar f=\sum_j a_jf_j$, $v_j=u_j- ar u$, and $R=\sum_j a_jv_j\otimes v_j$, and use $(u\otimes v)_{rs}=u_rv_s$ with rowwise tensor divergence. The exact finite weighted identity is $$\partial_t ar u+\operatorname{div}( ar u\otimes ar u)+
abla ar p=
u\Delta ar u+ ar f-\operatorname{div}R.$$ This is an identity for the specified smooth fields and fixed finite weights. It is not a probability-space expectation or a long-time average $T^{-1}\int_0^T u(t,x)\,dt$, and it does not identify either operation with the other. The tensor $R$ is the covariance term left by the nonlinear product; a closure prescription is an additional model relation that specifies this unresolved term using selected mean fields or additional variables. The identity itself supplies no such prescription. This remark asserts no measured turbulent flow, statistical averaging theorem, closure law, scaling law, universality result, or existence theorem for turbulent solutions.

references.title: Glenn Flierl and Raffaele Ferrari, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.820, Turbulence in the Ocean and Atmosphere, Chapter 3 (Spring 2006 lecture notes)
H. Tennekes and J. L. Lumley, A First Course in Turbulence (1972), full-text digital copy

items.physical_scope: Formal finite weighted averaging of smooth incompressible model fields and contextual limits on closure claims. No statistical averaging theorem, empirical turbulence observation, closure law, scaling law, or universality result is asserted.

items.title: Covariance versus effective Reynolds stress
items.design_state: Step 1 conditional argument complete; F01 carrier placement/readiness remains unresolved.
items.statement: Let $\tau>0$ seconds, $I=(-\tau,\tau)$, and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open region with $C^1$ boundary and $U$ an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. Choose a unit vector $e\in\mathbb R^3$ and a speed $c>0$ measured in m s$^{-1}$. On the reference neighborhood define $\chi_1(t,a)=a+ct e$ and $\chi_2(t,a)=a-ct e$, and on the open fluid domain $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$ set $u_1(t,x)=ce$ and $u_2(t,x)=-ce$. Take equal weights $a_1=a_2=1/2$, zero pressure and forcing fields $p_j=f_j=0$, and common $\nu=0$ in the finite Reynolds identity. For the formal constant-density interpretation, adopt a constant density parameter $\rho_0>0$ in kg m$^{-3}$. Define the covariance $R=\sum_{j=1}^2a_j(u_j-\bar u)\otimes(u_j-\bar u)$ and define the effective Reynolds-stress correction $\sigma_R=-\rho_0R$ when the momentum equation is written with a $+\operatorname{div}\sigma$ contribution on the right. Then $\bar u=0$, $R=c^2e\otimes e$, and $\rho_0R$ is a nonzero positive-semidefinite tensor with units Pa, while $\sigma_R$ has the opposite sign. This is an exact finite-field illustration, not an empirical observation or a statistical turbulence model.

references.title: Glenn Flierl and Raffaele Ferrari, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.820, Turbulence in the Ocean and Atmosphere, Chapter 3 (Spring 2006 lecture notes)
H. Tennekes and J. L. Lumley, A First Course in Turbulence (1972), full-text digital copy

items.physical_scope: A two-member constant-velocity example in a formal constant-density incompressible model, used only to distinguish covariance from the signed effective stress contribution and to check SI units. It reports no measurement and proposes no closure law.
